channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Europe: Extreme weather weighs on growth – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Christopher Graham and Emily Ashford highlight that Europe’s record heat and drought in 2026 are disrupting refiners, power generation, inland waterways and agriculture.

item.title: Food inflation jumped to 5.52% and the Reserve Bank of India held at 5.25%: Why rate hikes are still on the table
item.description: India’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation accelerated slightly to 4.45% year-on-year in July from 4.38% in June, primarily propelled by rising food costs.

item.title: United Kingdom: Growth risks tilt higher – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Sanjay Raja notes that the UK economy remained strong over spring, with UK GDP rising 0.4% q/q and annualised growth in the first half reaching 2%.

item.title: Gold struggles below two-month high despite softer US PPI
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades under pressure on Thursday after hitting a fresh two-month high of $4,449 during Asian trading hours. The metal fails to capitalise on softer-than-expected US Producer Price Index (PPI) data, even as the US Dollar and Treasury yields edge lower.

item.title: Norges Bank: Disinflation slows rate path – Nomura
item.description: Nomura economists note Norges Bank kept its policy rate at 4.25% in August despite softer CPI-ATE inflation. The bank still flags a possible further hike, but they now expect a November move, with risks tilted to no additional increase and no rate cuts projected until September 2027.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Trump pressure and rate risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank's Dr. Marco Wagner analyzes how Donald Trump’s past and potential future attacks on the Federal Reserve (Fed) affect its independence.

item.title: US Dollar: Yield support erodes on weaker inflation – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee notes that softer US CPI and labour data kept DXY locked in a 99.4–100.1 range after the USD/JPY sell-off linked to joint US-Japan interventions. Markets sharply reduced the implied probability of a September Federal Reserve hike.

item.title: "Still an open question": Fed’s Barkin keeps possibility of rate hike alive
item.description: Richmond Federal Reserve (Fed) President Thomas Barkin highlighted on Thursday the persistent uncertainty surrounding the US inflation outlook and monetary policy.

item.title: Euro: Choppy range trading outlook against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses EUR/USD dynamics in light of shifting Fed rate hike expectations and Oil-related safe haven flows into the Dollar.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy support for BoJ hikes – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights USD/JPY trading just below 160.00 as Japan’s government signals support for faster Bank of Japan (BoJ) rate hikes, reinforcing narrowing US–Japan differentials and a lower USD/JPY case.

item.title: Turkish Lira: Further depreciation seen against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank FX analyst Tatha Ghose highlights persistent inflation pressures and renewed current account deterioration as key drivers for continued weakness in the Turkish Lira against the Dollar.

item.title: US PPI comes in softer than expected, confirms easing inflation pressure
item.description: Producer inflation in the United States (US) cooled more than expected in July, adding to evidence that inflationary pressure is gradually easing after Wednesday's Consumer Price Index (CPI) data.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Gradual tightening path into 2027 – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Taylor Schleich and Ethan Currie reaffirm their Bank of Canada (BoC) rate call, arguing that despite stronger Canadian labour data and robust Q2 GDP, accumulated slack and data lags should delay tightening.

item.title: US Initial Jobless Claims increased to 209K last week
item.description: According to a report from the US Department of Labour (DOL) released on Thursday, the number of US citizens submitting new applications for unemployment insurance rose to 209K for the week ending August 8.

item.title: WTI Oil Price Forecast: Momentum turns flat as Bollinger Bands expand
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil trades modestly lower on Thursday as traders weigh weaker demand forecasts from OPEC and the International Energy Agency (IEA) against supply disruptions in the Middle East. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $80.50 per barrel, down 1.35% on the day.

item.title: Euro steadies against Japanese Yen as ECB rate hike expectations strengthen
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 183.80 on Thursday at the time of writing, little changed on the day.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Benign inflation reinforces RBI pause – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Radhika Rao analyzes India’s July inflation data and its implications for the Reserve Bank of India. She notes that benign core inflation and limited spillovers from external shocks support a continued RBI policy pause.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Anchored expectations back RBNZ hikes – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes NZD/USD briefly dipped below its 200-day moving average as the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) Q3 inflation expectations survey showed mixed but well-anchored readings near the 2% midpoint.

item.title: Euro gains against British Pound despite stronger UK growth data
item.description: EUR/GBP edges higher on Thursday as the Euro (EUR) draws support from hawkish European Central Bank (ECB) expectations, overshadowing stronger-than-expected UK Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data that would otherwise have supported the British Pound (GBP).

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD stands tall at two-month highs above $4,380
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) posts marginal losses on Thursday, after meeting resistance at the $4,450 area, yet with price action holding just above previous highs around $ 4,380 at the time of writing.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Gradual easing path – UOB
item.description: Alvin Liew of UOB outlines expectations for the Federal Funds Rate following the July US CPI release. Market pricing for a September hike has fallen, and UOB’s base case is an extended pause through 2026.

item.title: European Central Bank: Independence risks rise with debt – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Marco Wagner assesses how political pressure threatens the European Central Bank’s (ECB) independence using a Central Bank Pressure Index based on AI analysis of politicians’ statements.

item.title: Silver slips below $65, but cooling US inflation keeps downside in check
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades lower around $64.90 on Thursday at the time of writing, down 0.64% on the day. The white metal consolidates after its recent advance as investors refrain from taking large positions ahead of the release of US producer inflation data.

item.title: Riksbank: Rate hike risks rise – Nomura
item.description: Nomura strategists expects the Riksbank to keep its policy rate at 1.75% in August, with no change through 2026.

item.title: Indian Rupee drops despite lower US Dollar, oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) is under pressure against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday. The USD/INR pair rises to near 95.44 after a corrective move the previous day, even as the US Dollar and oil prices trade lower.

item.title: British Pound: Solid UK data, limited BoE impact – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes GBP/USD trading directionless near 1.3500 as United Kingdom (UK) Q2 and June Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data show encouraging activity. Growth was driven by investment and consumption, with government spending a drag.

item.title: British Pound recovers early losses against US Dollar, US PPI data eyed
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) claws back its early losses against the US Dollar (USD) and flattens at around 1.3495 during the European trading session on Thursday.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Norges Bank softens hawkish stance – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Norges Bank analysis notes the policy rate was left unchanged at 4.25% in August, with a less hawkish tone than in June.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Capped below the 50% retracement of July’s plunge, at 159.50
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) remains practically flat against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Thursday, as fading hopes of a Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike in September have undermined speculative demand for the Greenback.

item.title: Economists agree: ECB to hike interest rates by 25 bps to 2.5% in September - Reuters
item.description: According to a Reuters poll, the European Central Bank (ECB) will hike its deposit rates by 25 basis points (bps) to 2.50% in September, said 57 of 69 economists.
